parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by centripetal acceleration.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
(b) An unpowered toy car moves freely along a smooth track that is initially horizontal. The track contains a vertical circular loop around which the car travels, as shown in Fig. 1.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The mass of the car is 30 g and the diameter of the loop is 62 cm. Assume that the resistive forces acting on the car are negligible.
parts.text: State what happens to the magnitude of the centripetal acceleration of the car as it moves around the loop from X to Y.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, if the car remains in contact with the track, why the centripetal acceleration of the car at point Y must be greater than 9.8 m s⁻².

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The initial speed at which the car in (b) moves along the track is 3.8 m s⁻¹.

Determine whether the car is in contact with the track at point Y. Show your working.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Suggest, with a reason but without calculation, whether your conclusion in (c) would be different for a car of mass 460 g moving with the same initial speed.

figures.caption: Fig. 1.1
figures.alt: A toy car on a horizontal track beside a vertical circular loop, with X at the bottom and Y at the top, arrows showing motion around the loop and a 62 cm diameter measurement.
